1941-07-24.ocr: ESTABLISHED By SAMUEL BOWLUS WEEKLY IN 1824 DAILY IN 1844 SUNDAY IN 1878 EDITORIAL DISCUSSION OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL EVENTS Of Course Its an Alliance To so blunt and downright a statesman as Winston Churchill it must be a relief to discard the thin pretense that the AngloRussian pact is something else than an al liance It is of course an al liance the British prime minister told the House of Commons Tues day and the Russian people are now our allies But while this preference for plain speaking needs no explanation we are still left to guess why the British government abruptly reversed its policy A possible explanation might be that British opinion had taken so kindly to the link with Moscow that calling it an association was seen to be unnecessary With the war at so critical a stage even the most bitter opponents of what Lloyd George once called shaking hands with murder have been delighted by the unlookedfor strength of the Russian defense and are perhaps readier to believe that the Moscow government whatever its defects represents the Russian peopleat any rate during the emergency to which the alliance is limited General approval of the pact
